case.component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
case.narrative: The rear view parking camera software is defective.  If you put the car into reverse, the rear parking camera view comes up (as intended). However, if you put the car into drive and then back into reverse (as if you are making some parking adjustments in a parking lot), the rear parking camera view does NOT come back up.   In fact, it requires several additional touches on the car's infotainment touchscreen to bring the rear parking camera view back up.

decision.rationale: Safety flag stands; the case keeps priority for a live engineer.

proposal.rationale: The narrative describes a repeatable software behaviour: the rear camera displays on the first shift into reverse, but after shifting to drive and back to reverse the image does not return and requires several infotainment touchscreen inputs to restore. This matches a camera-software display-restore defect on the 2025 Polestar 3, and an open recall (25V293000) for the same model/year addresses a rearview camera image that may not display in reverse, citing FMVSS 111 rear visibility non-compliance. No rulebook entry or prior similar case is available, so a standard functional verification of the camera display on repeated reverse engagements is proposed rather than a rulebook-named targeted test. Because loss of the rear camera view while reversing can deprive the driver of rear visibility and create a back-over risk, the case is flagged for human review before any test is booked.
proposal.summary: Safety-relevant: send to an engineer before any test is booked

recalls.summary: Polestar Automotive USA, Inc. (Polestar) is recalling certain Polestar 3 vehicles.  The rearview camera image may not display when the vehicle is placed in reverse.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 111, "Rear Visibility."
